claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing a controlled density of nanoscale precipitates within the lamellar colonies will improve strength.
Introducing a controlled density of nanoscale precipitates within the lamellar colonies will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
Nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase strength.
Nanoscale precipitates will reduce stress concentrations at internal boundaries.
Reduced stress concentrations at internal boundaries will enhance tensile ductility.
The precipitate-containing alloy will exhibit a 20% increase in yield strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The precipitate-containing alloy will exhibit a 30% increase in tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Successful operation of the intervention requires precipitates to be uniformly distributed within the lamellar colonies.
Successful operation of the intervention requires precipitate sizes between 10 and 50 nm.
The optimal precipitate density and size distribution are unknown.
The hypothesis is falsified if yield strength increases by less than 10% or tensile ductility increases by less than 20% relative to the unmodified control.
